J U D G M E N T :

1.0 Vide this appeal, the appellants have challenged order dated 18.03.2016 ("the impugned order" in short) passed by Ld. Adjudicating Officer/Additional District Magistrate (North District) ("ADM" in short), directing Sh.Rajender Kumar S/o Late Bansi Lal, M/s Madan Store, A1, Gujrawalan Town, Delhi110009 to pay penalty of Rs.50,000/ and the above appellants namely Sh.Satya Pal, Sh.Sunil Aggarwal,partners M/s Adarsh Suppliers Company and the firm to pay penalty of Rs.1,50,000/, under Section 52 of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 ("FSS Act"
Satya Pal S/O Late Pralad Raj vs D.V.Singh on 25 October, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175722834/
1 in short) for violation of Regulation 2.2.2.10 of The Food Safety &
Standards (Packaging & Labeling) Regulations, 2011 ("FSS (P&L)
Regulations" in short). 
2.0

Briefly stating the facts relevant for disposal  appeal are that:
 (i) on 9th July, 2015, Food Safety Officer ("FSO" in  short), purchased 4 sealed packets of "Haldi Powder"
FSAT No. 40/16  Satya Pal & Ors. vs Food Safety Officer  from Sh.Rajender Kumar, s/o Late Sh.Bansi Lal of M/s  Madan Store, A1 Gujranwala Town, Delhi  110009(Food Business Operator)(FBO), where the said  food article was found stored for sale for h  consumption.

sentences.text: 4.0 On the other hand, Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor for the State submitted that this appeal is not maintainable as the appellants pleaded guilty before the Ld. Trial Court.
They cannot now raise the contentions as raised by them in their appeals.
Even otherwise, they have no case on merits as the label did not meet the requirements of Regulation 2.2.2.10 of FSS (P&L) Regulation.
5.0 I have heard Sh.R.K.Ahuja,Ld.Advocate for the appellants and Sh. Anil, Ld. Chief PP for the State and have perused the record carefully.

Satya Pal S/O Late Pralad Raj vs D.V.Singh on 25 October, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175722834/

6.0
Perusal of the record show that the sample of "Haldi Powder" was purchased from Sh.Rajender Kumar S/o Late Sh.Bansi Lal, of M/s Madan Store, A1, Gujrawalan Town Delhi 110009 on 09.07.2015.
Food Analyst vide his report dated 22.07.2015 reported the sample to be "misbranded" in view of violation of Regulation 2.2.2.10 of FSS (P&L) Regulation.

6.1 Let me refer to the regulation 2.2.2.10 FSS  Regulations, which requires the label to display the 'Best Before'
FSAT No. 40/16  Satya Pal & Ors. vs Food Safety Officer  and 'Use By' date.

The said regulation reads as under :
 "2.2.2 Labelling of Prepackaged  10 Best Before and Use by Da  (i) the month and year in capital letters upto wh  is best for consumption, in the following manner  "BEST BEFORE ........ MONTHS AND YEAR" 
 
 BEST BEFORE ....MONTHS FROM PACKAGING" 
 
 "BEST BEFORE ....MONTHS FROM MANUFACTURE"
6.2

Perusal of the Food Analyst's report dated 22.07.2015 shows that :
 ".....
 Analysis Report:
 (i) Sample Description: ADARSH subzi brand hal  sample in original sealed packet contained inside original  plain polythene packet.
 (ii).....
 (iii) Label:Best before language not declared in capital  .....
O p i n i o n : T h e s a m p l e i s m i s b r a n d e d b e c a u s e t h e r e i s v i o l a t i o n o f Regulation 2.2.2.10 of The Food Safety & Standards(Packaging & Labelling) Regulation, 2011.

"
S a t y a P a l & O r s . v s F o o d S a f e t y O f f i c e r 6 . 3 P e r u s a l o f t h e p a n c h n a m a r e v e a l s t h a t o n t h e l a b e l t h e required declaration read as under:
"Best Before six months after Packing Date"
Satya Pal S/O Late Pralad Raj vs D.V.Singh on 25 October, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175722834/
4 6 . 4 F r o m t h e a b o v e , i t i s e v i d e n t t h a t t h e l a b e l m e n t i o n e d a b o u t t h e p e r i o d u p t o w h i c h t h e s a m p l e f o o d c o m m o d i t y w a s b e s t f o r c o n s u m p t i o n t h o u g h , n o t i n t h e e x a c t p r e s c r i b e d f o r m . L e t m e m e n t i o n h e r e t h a t i n s o m e w h a t s i m i l a r s i t u a t i o n , t h e H o n ' b l e D e l h i H i g h C o u r t i n R a m B a b u R a s t o g i a n d o t h e r s V . S t a t e , T h r o u g h Food Inspector(PFA)2012(1) FAC 56, in para no. 14 observed as under :
"14.

The actual label found at the sample article i.e. "Best before within 6 months from date of packaging" conveyed much more than which was  required to be conveyed to the purchasers about the genuineness of the  product.
Mere use of word "within" as a surplusage would not bring the  petitioners under the penal provisions of the Act.
By any means, the  purchasers could not be said to have been deceived or misled as regards
the  character, quantity, quality or date of manufacture and the limit of use of the product

. " 
6.5 Further in the case law relied upon by the appellants, in M.D.Anand Aqua's case(Supra) as

w e l l a s i n O s c a r J o s e p h ' s S a t y a P a l & O r s . v s F o o d S a f e t y O f f i c e r c a s e ( S u p r a ) , t h e l a b e l d i d n o t m e n t i o n t h e w o r d s B E S T B E F O R E in capital letters and rather, mentioned it in small letters.
In that fact situation, the Hon'ble  Patna High Court noted that there was a sufficient compliance.

In  P r a m o d

,
similar view was taken by Hon'ble Patna High Court with respect to mentioning of   date of manufacturing and expiry in small letters though required to be written in capital letters.

6 . 6 A s n o t e d a b o v e , i n t h e i n s t a n t c a s e a l s o , t h e l a b e l o n t h e s a m p l e f o o d c o m m o d i t y m e n t i o n e d " B e s t B e f o r e s i x m o n t h s A f t e r P a c k i n g D a t e " , d i d c o n v e y t h e d a t e b y w h i c h i t w a s b e s t t o c o n s u m e the food article.
In view of the same and the position of law as discussed above, it can be  i n f e r r e d t h a t t h e l a b e l o n t h e s a m p l e commodity sufficiently complied with Regulation 2.2.2.10.
In view of the same, penalty imposed  by the Ld.ADM cannot be justified.
6.7 In view of the above, I need not go into other contentions raised by the appellants.
